inputs.text: Two Michigan middle-school brothers are taking their case to the U.S. Supreme Court after their school ordered them to remove hoodies bearing “Let’s Go Brandon.” The phrase came from a crowd shouting “F*** Joe Biden!” at a 2021 NASCAR event, only for an NBC interviewer to present it as “Let’s go Brandon!” That convenient sanitizing of the message says a lot: now lower courts are treating clothing that can be read as profane as grounds for a ban. This looks less like protecting students and more like institutions deciding which political speech is acceptable—and suppressing it when the message is too clear.

output.main_topic: Michigan middle-school brothers’ Supreme Court challenge to a school ban on hoodies bearing “Let’s Go Brandon”
